claims.text: Uniformly distributed TiC precipitates govern high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten-based alloys.
TiC precipitates stabilize dislocation motion and mitigate strain localization.
The proposed initial tungsten-rich alloy lacks a controlled dispersion of carbide phases.
Adding titanium during elemental powder mixing followed by spark plasma sintering causes in-situ TiC formation.
The resulting TiC precipitates occur both within grains and along grain boundaries.
Elemental powder mixing followed by spark plasma sintering can produce fine-grained, high-density material with controlled structure.
Uniformly dispersed TiC within grains and at grain boundaries is the structural mediator.
Increasing evenly distributed TiC in a tungsten matrix increases creep strength.
TiC raises the recrystallization temperature of tungsten-based material.
Carbides at tungsten grain boundaries strengthen the boundaries and resist grain-boundary migration at elevated temperature.
TiC precipitates provide barriers to dislocation motion.
TiC-induced strengthening suppresses strain localization and permits more uniform plastic deformation.
Suppression of strain localization delays crack initiation and improves elevated-temperature toughness.
The Ti-added alloy will exhibit greater high-temperature plastic strain than an otherwise identical alloy without controlled TiC precipitation.
The Ti-added alloy will exhibit delayed crack initiation and greater energy absorption than the baseline alloy.
A uniformly TiC-reinforced tungsten composite can withstand heat flux up to 200 MW/m2, nearly 100% above that sustained by pure tungsten.

The proposed plastic-strain and toughness mechanism should hold for fine-grained tungsten-based plasma-facing materials under fusion-relevant temperature and heat-flux conditions when TiC remains uniformly distributed.
The magnitude of mechanical improvement may depend on TiC volume fraction and distribution.
Irradiation and thermal cycling may alter the magnitude of the ductility and toughness improvement.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement in both high-temperature ductility and toughness, or observation of degraded performance, would falsify the hypothesis.
